title: Seasonal sea level remained linked to NHC surge-range errors after gauge and storm controls in 2017-2025
abstract: We tested the background-water attribution in a published check of NHC surge ranges. We used its table of 788 complete storm-gauge units, 45 storms and 122 gauges in 2017-2025. We added gauge and storm controls and split background sea level into a seasonal part and a prior 12-month mean. For the constructed high-tide outcome, the total-background slope was 0.97 feet per foot (storm-cluster 95% interval 0.21 to 1.74). In the parts model, the seasonal slope was 1.37 (0.47 to 2.27), while the prior-mean slope was 0.31 (-0.75 to 1.37). Intervals that also allowed shared gauge errors gave the same sign conclusions. Restricted wild-cluster tests and leave-one-storm checks supported the seasonal link. For actual observed peaks, the total-background interval included zero. The result strengthens the seasonal-background explanation, but does not isolate an omitted sea-level-rise term. The prior mean also contains interannual changes and datum effects. The analysis is retrospective and exploratory. Gauge values do not measure coastal-area maxima, and the high-tide outcome assumes additive tide and residual effects. We did not inspect operational initial conditions or test forecast improvements. The package includes the attributed published input, new code, all model estimates, diagnostics and a figure.

display.caption: Error slopes after gauge and storm controls. Intervals allow errors shared by storm and gauge. The seasonal part retains a positive link; the prior-mean slope remains uncertain. Blue lines show nominal 95% intervals; the grey line is zero and the orange line is one.

citations.reason: We reuse and attribute its published storm-gauge table. New gauge and storm controls refine the background attribution; no new independent observation sample.
